related_questions.question: What is the rate of inflation since 2005?

text_blocks.snippet: Between 2005 and 2025, the average annual inflation rate in the US was 2.52%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics In2013dollars.com. This means that cumulative price increases over the 20-year period reached 64.60%. In other words, prices in 2025 are about 1.65 times higher than they were in 2005.

related_questions.question: When was the worst inflation in the United States?

text_blocks.snippet: The worst inflation in U.S. history, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), occurred in 1917, with a year-over-year rate of 20.49%. This period was marked by the aftermath of World War I and the subsequent surge in prices for goods and services.

list.title: 1917: The Peak:
list.snippet: The year 1917 saw the highest inflation rate since the CPI's inception, with prices rising by over 20%.

list.title: Post-WWI Inflation:
list.snippet: The period following World War I (1918-1920) also experienced high inflation, with prices increasing by more than 80% from late 1916 to mid-1920.

list.title: Causes:
list.snippet: The primary drivers of this inflation were the increased demand for resources due to the war effort and subsequent supply shortages.

list.title: Government Response:
list.snippet: The Federal Reserve (before it had a unified national policy) attempted to combat inflation by raising interest rates, but this led to a recession.

list.title: Historical Context:
list.snippet: While 1917 is the highest in the CPI era, the highest year-over-year inflation rate ever recorded in the U.S. was 29.78% in 1778, during the Revolutionary War.
